speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our assessment of your chest skin lesion, can you tell me how long you have had it and if it has changed in size, color, or shape?

speaker: Patient
text: 63-year-old male. The patient reports noticing a skin lesion on his chest 2 months ago, which he believes has increased in size. He denies any associated pain or itching with the lesion. He has a medical history significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and glaucoma.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see; given your history of diabetes and the lesion's growth over two months, have you noticed any bleeding, crusting, or ulceration on it? Additionally, does the lesion have an irregular border or multiple colors?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin lesion on the chest. I also have Lesion has increased in size, Not painful, Not itchy.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma. Given the lesion's location, rapid growth over two months, lack of pain/itch, and your history of diabetes and age, this is highly suspicious for SCC. I recommend an urgent biopsy and excision to confirm the diagnosis and stage the tumor. REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of chest lesion. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy of chest lesion.
